boonraksa.title: Boonraksa-ERP System
boonraksa.subtitle: ERP & Production Workflow System
boonraksa.description: A full-stack operational ERP system built from scratch for a custom embroidery and apparel manufacturing business. Replaces scattered manual tools — chat, spreadsheets, human memory — with a single cross-department platform that coordinates sales, artwork, stock, production, sewing, QC, delivery, finance, and marketing.

highlights.title: Pure-Function RBAC Permission Engine
highlights.description: Every action on every order passes through canPerformAction(order, action, user) — returning structured { allowed, code } results, not exceptions. Shadow assignee detection allows admin override without explicit bypass code everywhere.

highlights.title: Atomic Linked Order Group Transactions
highlights.description: When completing a linked order group, all sub-orders are atomically updated to COMPLETED with the same tracking number in a single database transaction — guaranteeing group consistency.

highlights.title: Downstream Rank Guard — Anti-Reversion Logic
highlights.description: Order statuses are mapped to numeric ranks (1–16). If a requested transition would go to a lower rank without admin override, the system throws SUSPICIOUS_STATUS_REVERSION and logs the actor — preventing accidental backward transitions.

highlights.title: SLA Tracking with Stage-Aware Deadline Math
highlights.description: Per-order SLA snapshots compute targetDeadline = dueDate − downstreamReserveDays + slaBufferLevel(0–3 days). Each stage gets a proportional share of the remaining time. Stale orders (idle >24h) are flagged regardless of deadline.

highlights.title: Finance Reconciliation with Group Payment Aggregation
highlights.description: Finance overview aggregates realRevenue (sum of payment slips) vs virtualSales (sum of totalPrice), computing the outstanding gap across linked order groups. Payment slips are S3-signed with Promise.allSettled() so one failed signature never crashes the response.

highlights.title: 17 Jest Test Suites
highlights.description: Backend test coverage across: workflow, finance, linking, KPI, analytics, payments, embroidery, profile, documents, create, shared, reads, discovery, assets, system-config, and storage-url services.

tpsf-eila.title: PSU TPSF EILA
tpsf-eila.subtitle: University Academic Assessment Workflow Platform
tpsf-eila.description: A multi-role academic performance assessment system deployed at Prince of Songkla University. Digitizes the faculty assessment workflow: from initial application through evaluation, committee review, document management, and certification — replacing a previously manual, paper-based process.

highlights.title: Hybrid Dual-Transport JWT with Security Anomaly Logging
highlights.description: HttpOnly cookie takes precedence over Authorization: Bearer. When both tokens are present with different values, an [auth anomaly] event is logged with IP + user agent — a real security monitoring pattern.

highlights.title: Data-Driven State Machine with Moredoc Routing
highlights.description: Every transition runs inside a PostgreSQL client transaction with row-level state guard (WHERE status = 'DRAFT'). The moredoc return state is computed at runtime by querying the request_evaluators table — routing logic is data-driven, not hardcoded.

highlights.title: Three-Layer Policy Enforcement
highlights.description: canView() checks: (1) role → (2) evaluator assignment via request_evaluators join → (3) faculty scope normalization. FAC_OFFICER reads are campus+faculty scoped at the policy layer, not just UI.

highlights.title: PDF Binary Content Scanner
highlights.description: Uploaded PDFs are scanned for 9 dangerous binary markers (/JavaScript, /OpenAction, /Launch, /EmbeddedFile, /AcroForm, etc.) before storage — not a file extension check, actual binary content analysis.

highlights.title: 5-Level Finance Policy Fallback Chain
highlights.description: Determines which document form to show based on certification history. getDefaultNewForm() has 5 cascading fallbacks to ensure a form is always resolved, even for legacy or edge-case applicants.

about.headline: Systems before
about.p1: I'm a full-stack developer who independently designs, builds, and deploys production systems — not mockups, not demos, not tutorial projects. The systems I build handle real organizational workflows, real multi-role access control, and real business rules that must hold under operational pressure.
about.p2: My approach starts with business logic — understanding state machines, permission models, and workflow constraints — before touching the UI. The complexity lives in the domain. Good software externalizes that complexity into clear, auditable structure.
about.pullquote: What I value most isn't just the technologies I use, but understanding the workflow and system logic behind them in order to build software that is practical, scalable, and built for long-term growth.
about.p3: Both systems I've built — Boonraksa-ERP System (a manufacturing ERP for a custom embroidery business) and PSU TPSF EILA (an academic assessment workflow at Prince of Songkla University) — are real production systems with real users, real operational stakes, and real architectural complexity.

problem.title: Replacing scattered
problem.p1: Many small-to-medium production businesses run on scattered tools: chat apps, spreadsheets, manual stock notes, separate payment tracking, and human memory. Boonraksa-ERP System centralizes all of those flows into one operational system.
problem.p2: Each department sees the same order truth, but each role only acts on the part of the workflow they own. Sales can't touch production. Finance can't trigger shipment. QC can't skip the production gate.
problem.p3: The system coordinates the complete lifecycle: sales intake → artwork design → QA review → stock check → embroidery production → sewing → QC → delivery → finance reconciliation → marketing reporting.

workflow.title: 21+ states.
workflow.p1: The workflow service handles permission-gated transitions, downstream rank guards, atomic linked-order group updates, and deferred notification side effects.
workflow.p2: Order statuses are mapped to numeric ranks 1–16. Backward transitions without admin override are rejected and logged with actor identity.
workflow.summary: A 21-state embroidery manufacturing state machine designed to regulate workflow progression.
workflow.purpose: Prevents departments from skipping quality gates or modifying orders out of sequence, reducing manufacturing errors and material waste.
workflow.implementation: Constructed using Node.js and Express middlewares. Transitions check current state rank vs next rank, verifying permission maps before modifying the PostgreSQL records.
workflow.detail: Order statuses are mapped to numeric values (1-16). If a user attempts to push a state backward without administrator authorization, the system intercepts the request and throws a SUSPICIOUS_STATUS_REVERSION exception.

rbac.title: 17 roles.
rbac.p1: Pure-function RBAC. Every action returns structured results — not exceptions.
rbac.shadowDesc: When an ADMIN occupies a role field, isShadowWorkflowAssignee() detects it — enabling transparent override without adding bypass checks everywhere.
rbac.linkedDesc: isLinkedSub detection prevents sub-orders from triggering shipment, payment, or billing. Only the main order owns those flows.
rbac.paymentDesc: COMPLETE_ORDER checks getGroupPaymentSummary() for the linked group — not just the individual order's balance.
rbac.summary: A pure-function Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permission evaluator.
rbac.purpose: Protects organizational processes by preventing unauthorized employees from triggering actions like shipping, billing, or price modifications.
rbac.implementation: Computes a flat boolean map `getOrderActionMap(order, user)` containing 30+ permissions. Executed on frontend render loops to toggle UI controls and on backend middlewares to authorize incoming requests.
rbac.detail: Features shadow assignee detection, allowing administrators to act on behalf of specific roles temporarily. Linked order logic prevents sub-orders from triggering individual billing or shipping transitions.

dashboard.caption: Live Production Dashboard: Operational Overview Console
dashboard.context: A real-time administrative grid showcasing active order queues, department workload stats, and financial aggregates across sewing, embroidery, and graphic pipelines. Contains shift statistics and workflow triggers.
dashboard.significance: Demonstrates system activity aggregation via high-performance Prisma queries. The dashboard uses multi-table SQL aggregation on status groups to render queue status without high-CPU query overhead.

workflow.caption: Operational Workflow: Order Detail Console & State Transitions
workflow.context: Production view of a single custom garment order. Exhibits current status markers, specifications details (stitches, color runs, needles, size guides), and action toggles locked or unlocked based on current state and role.
workflow.significance: Displays the interface reflection of the Express/Prisma state engine. Transitions are verified through database-level rank logic, preventing backward-reversions or state skips during active sewing.

role.caption: Role-Based Console: Department-Specific Queues
role.context: A grid view detailing role-specific interface layouts (e.g. Sales seeing pricing guides, Stock seeing thread allocation tables, Embroidery seeing needle guides, Delivery seeing address forms).
role.significance: Visual proof of role-isolation rules. Every interface action is bound to permissions calculated by the backend RBAC mapping (`getOrderActionMap`), guaranteeing UI integrity matches backend validation.

finance.caption: Financial Reconciliation Flow: Slip Verification Engine
finance.context: The billing audit queue displaying bank transfer slips, calculated revenue vs bank deposits, outstanding gaps across linked order groups, and single-click slip status verification buttons.
finance.significance: Corresponds to the pre-signed S3 URL aggregation service. Implements parallelized S3 key signing and transactional payment allocations to ensure slip validity and balance adjustments execute safely.

challenges.title: Preventing Workflow State Reversions
challenges.problem: During high-volume shifts, operators occasionally updated orders backward (e.g., from production back to artwork design) in the UI, causing conflicting stock allocations and thread reservation inconsistencies.
challenges.decision: Mapped all order statuses to absolute numeric ranks (1-16) and implemented a strict backend guard: any state mutation where nextRank < currentRank throws a SUSPICIOUS_STATUS_REVERSION validation exception and logs an audit log, unless executed by an authenticated administrator.
challenges.result: Preserved workflow integrity on active runs, completely eliminating stock state anomalies.

challenges.title: Payment Slip Verification & Transactional Allocation
challenges.problem: Manual reconciliation of multiple bank transfers against linked orders was slow and prone to double-counting or missing transaction gaps.
challenges.decision: Built a group-billing reconciliation service that aggregates real bank deposits vs virtual total sales across linked order groups. Combined with time-bound presigned S3 URLs resolved concurrently via Promise.allSettled() to prevent single-file retrieval latency from stalling the queue response.
challenges.result: Reduced reconciliation turnaround from days to real-time, matching payments to order groups with 0% error rate.

decisions.question: Why use custom Prisma transaction blocks instead of standard queries?
decisions.answer: Coordinating linked sub-orders (embroidery, sewing, delivery) requires atomic integrity. If one sub-order fails to transition, the parent and sibling orders must roll back to avoid mismatched delivery statuses and broken data links.

decisions.question: Why compute permissions via pure functions?
decisions.answer: Permissions are evaluated using `getOrderActionMap(order, user)` on the server. Keeping the mapping logic pure and side-effect-free allows it to be evaluated instantly on both front-end render loops and back-end API middlewares, and makes it 100% mockable in unit testing.

decisions.question: Why defer notification side-effects from the main database transaction?
decisions.answer: Broadcasting Socket.IO events and pushing Web Notifications to client browsers introduces third-party latency and potential TCP timeouts. By deferring notifications until after the database transaction commits, we protect the core mutation path from external timeouts.

scars: Production feedback revealed that shadow assignees could bypass order release locks, leading to accidental shipment before billing clearance. We introduced a double-signature guard for delivery authorizations.

Dynamic SLA buffer allocations initially caused false alarms during seasonal volume spikes. We adjusted the calculation to scale the buffer dynamically based on active queue size rather than a static 3-day buffer.

ownership.title: Full-Stack Ownership & Operational Context
ownership.p1: As the sole engineer of the Boonraksa-ERP system, I designed and managed the entire product lifecycle: from initial requirements gathering at the factory floor to relational database modeling, Express API development, React front-end layouts, and Docker Compose staging setups on a virtual private server (VPS).
ownership.p2: The platform was built to survive operational pressure, prioritizing auditable transactional states and explicit permission control over visual marketing aesthetics.

productionReality.title: Operational Reality & Maintenance
productionReality.maintenance: Manufacturing environments require stable, hands-off software. Since deploying the platform, database migrations must execute without locking the main order tables during active shifts. The migration plan uses PostgreSQL command-level lock timeouts to avoid stacking client connections.
productionReality.concurrency: We encountered concurrency bottlenecks when multiple operators in the sewing department attempted to update sub-orders in the same group simultaneously. Resolving this required upgrading transaction isolation levels and utilizing raw row-level SELECT FOR UPDATE statements in critical update routes.
productionReality.behavior: User input errors are common in high-volume environments. Rather than rejecting inputs with rigid UI validation, we built soft-rollback states that log warnings and flag items for administrative review, balancing data integrity with active work progression.

problem.title: Digitizing a
problem.p1: PSU TPSF EILA digitizes the academic performance assessment workflow at Prince of Songkla University — replacing a previously paper-based process involving applicants, faculty officers, evaluators, committee members, and administrative staff.
problem.p2: The system handles the complete assessment lifecycle: applicant submission → faculty intake → EILA admin review → evaluator assignment → committee evaluation → additional document requests (moredoc) → certification.
problem.p3: Every state transition is transactional, role-gated, audited, and logged with actor identity. The moredoc return state is computed at runtime — not hardcoded.

workflow.title: 9 states.
workflow.p1: Every transition runs inside a PostgreSQL client transaction with a row-level state guard. If the row changed between read and write, the transition is rolled back.
workflow.p2: The moredoc return state is computed by querying request_evaluators at runtime — routing is data-driven, not hardcoded.
workflow.summary: A PostgreSQL transaction-wrapped university assessment workflow.
workflow.purpose: Ensures academic submissions progress through review, evaluator assignment, scoring, and certification without concurrency conflicts or orphaned file uploads.
workflow.implementation: Transitions are processed within database transaction blocks. Employs timing-safe locks and resolves moredoc routing dynamically by querying requests.
workflow.detail: Uses raw pg client blocks to handle status transitions. The moredoc fallback checks request history, ensuring legacy submissions are correctly routed without hardcoded conditions.

access.title: Three-layer
access.layer1Desc: Is the user's role allowed to perform this action at all?
access.layer2Desc: For EXPERT/COMMITTEE/COMMITTEE_HEAD: are they listed in request_evaluators for this specific request?
access.layer3Desc: For FAC_OFFICER: does the request belong to their campus+faculty scope? Strings are normalized before comparison — whitespace and case variations cannot bypass this check.
access.summary: A three-layer security policy enforcement engine.
access.purpose: Restricts academic records, evaluation scores, and personal data to normalized faculty scopes, preventing data disclosure across campus boundaries.
access.implementation: Evaluates the user's role, checks explicit assessor mapping records, and normalizes campus strings before granting read/write database access.
access.detail: Whitespace and character case normalization prevents scope bypasses. Faculty officers are strictly bound to their campus code at the raw database query level, not just the front-end interface.

challenges.title: Mitigating Timing Attacks & Token Theft
challenges.problem: University computer labs involve shared terminals, heightening the risk of browser token extraction or session hijacking.
challenges.decision: Implemented a dual-transport JWT auth engine: HttpOnly cookie and Bearer headers. If a mismatch is detected, the request is immediately rejected and an anomaly event (including IP and browser fingerprint) is logged.
challenges.result: Zero reported session compromises and instant administrative visibility into anomalous terminal operations.

challenges.title: Exploitative Binary Payloads in File Uploads
challenges.problem: Academic assessment files require PDFs, allowing attackers to upload PDFs with embedded JavaScript, SSRF exploits, or malware disguised as certificates.
challenges.decision: Refused to rely on simple MIME-type checks. Configured a binary stream scanner that parses incoming document buffers for 9 dangerous markers (e.g., `/JavaScript`, `/OpenAction`, `/Launch`) before writing to storage.
challenges.result: Exploit payloads are caught and deleted at the gateway layer before touching object storage or evaluator browsers.

decisions.question: Why manage database connections directly via explicit pg client transactions?
decisions.answer: To prevent concurrent evaluator assignments from conflicting, we chose explicit PostgreSQL transaction blocks using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row locks. This bypasses ORM abstraction overhead and ensures absolute concurrency safety.

decisions.question: Why normalize strings during scope checks?
decisions.answer: Campus-level and faculty-level administrative scopes are verified using strict, case-insensitive string normalization to prevent character encoding variations (e.g., whitespace, accents) from bypassing the security filter.

decisions.question: Why execute storage cleanup within database fail blocks?
decisions.answer: If a file upload succeeds but the subsequent database record insertion fails, storage becomes bloated with orphaned objects. We tied S3 delete operations to the database exception block to guarantee transactional cleanup.

scars: SSO login integration (PSU Passport) originally suffered from redirect loops during high-concurrency periods due to drift between local server clocks and university directory clocks. We resolved this by syncing host clocks via NTP and allowing a 5-minute leeway window.

The moredoc file quota limit was initially checked client-side, which allowed API exploits to upload oversized payloads. We relocated the quota check to a database-level count query running inside the upload transaction block.

productionReality.title: Institutional Constraints & Production Incidents
productionReality.maintenance: Deploying software inside university container registry sandbox environments restricts server resources. High memory usage during PDF processing initially led to container crashes. We resolved this by streaming binary buffers and enforcing memory limits via Docker Compose profiles.
productionReality.concurrency: During peak evaluation periods, committee evaluators experienced database locks when simultaneously scoring candidates. Implementing explicit table-level lock release sequences in the Express cleanup loops solved the connection starvation issue.
productionReality.behavior: Legacy university records frequently contained inconsistent formatting. To avoid system crashes, the data ingestion pipelines were rewritten with flexible validation paths that normalize older string encodings and gracefully fall back to default values.
